quotes.text: A Fabric app is a managed web application that runs inside Microsoft Fabric. That word "managed" is the key. It means Fabric handles the hard parts, so you don't have to.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concise definition of Fabric apps and its core value.

quotes.text: So when you hear goodbye Power BI, what people really mean is, hello, more options. They're not saying Power BI is dead, they're saying they have another way to build on their data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defuses the hype that Fabric apps replaces Power BI.

quotes.text: Your skills become more valuable, not less. Data modeling, DAX, understanding business logic, these are the foundation that makes Fabric apps work.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reassures Power BI professionals that their skills carry over.

quotes.text: Without a good semantic model, your Fabric app has nothing to connect to. The people who understand the data will be the ones building the best apps.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Positions the semantic model as the foundation for apps.

quotes.text: Fabric apps is powerful, but it's not a silver bullet. Go in with realistic expectations. Use it for internal tools, prototypes, and apps where you control authentication.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Offers a balanced recommendation on where Fabric apps fits today.

chapters.title: Is this the end of Power BI?

takeaways: Fabric apps is a managed web app item in Fabric that bundles a SQL database, a GraphQL API, Entra ID authentication and static hosting.
Fabric apps complements rather than replaces Power BI, with both building on the same governed semantic model as the single source of truth.
The feature is in public preview, limited to internal Entra ID users and consumes Fabric capacity, so start with a small internal use case.
hook: Social media claims Fabric apps will replace Power BI, but the reality is more nuanced. This episode explains for Power BI and Fabric users what a Fabric app is, how it connects to semantic models and SQL data, and where its limits are. You will know when to build an app, when to stick with a report and how to get started.
